faq: Will you change my original file?
No. We work on a copy and keep your original untouched. Every edit is recorded in a change log, so you can see exactly what moved and undo anything you disagree with.
How do you decide what counts as a duplicate?
We agree the matching rules with you first, for example same email or same name and postcode. Uncertain matches are listed for you to approve instead of being merged automatically.
Can you fill in missing values?
We can fill gaps from other columns in your own data when the rule is clear, such as country from postcode. We do not invent or buy data to fill gaps, and unclear gaps are listed for you.
What file types can you clean?
CSV, Excel and Google Sheets are the easiest. We can also clean exports from your store, CRM or email tool as long as you can download them as a table.
desc:
Data cleaning for spreadsheets and customer lists fixes duplicates, mixed formats and gaps so your tables are ready to use. Ecom Swift LLC cleans a copy of your data and returns a tidy file with a change log of every edit.

## What is data cleaning?

Data cleaning is the careful correction of a table so that each row means one thing and each column follows one format. It covers removing repeated records, trimming stray spaces, unifying date styles, standardizing phone numbers and marking missing values. The goal is a table that can be sorted, filtered, merged and imported without surprises.

Cleaning is not guessing. Where a value cannot be fixed safely, we mark it for follow-up rather than invent an answer.

## Why messy lists quietly cost you

A customer list built over several years usually holds the same person three times, with different spellings and an old email address. A product sheet may have prices typed with commas in some rows and points in others. Dates arrive as day first from one export and month first from another.

These faults hide until you try to use the data. An email campaign goes twice to the same person. A pivot table splits one city into four spellings. An import into a store or CRM fails halfway and leaves partial records. Each problem is small, but together they waste hours and weaken any report built on top.

## How clean data improves your work

Clean data makes every later step cheaper. Counts become honest, because one customer is one row. Mail merges address people correctly. Imports into accounting, store or marketing tools run without rejected lines. Filters and lookups behave the same way every time.

It also makes handover easier. A new colleague can open a consistent table and understand it at once, instead of learning its quirks. How much time you save depends on how messy the source is and how often you export new data, which is why a repeatable process is worth considering.

## What a good cleaning job includes

- Work on a copy, with your original file left untouched.
- Removal of leading, trailing and double spaces, and consistent upper and lower case in names.
- One date format across the whole sheet, with ambiguous dates raised with you first.
- Exact duplicates removed and near-duplicates, such as a name with a typo, matched for your decision.
- Phone, address and country values written in one pattern.
- Email addresses checked for obvious faults such as missing symbols.
- Empty or suspicious cells listed so someone can follow up.
- A change log showing each altered, merged or deleted row and the rule behind it.
- A short list of the rules, approved by you before changes are made.

## How we work

You send the file and tell us what it is used for. We look through it, write down the rules we propose, and show you examples of what would change. Only after you approve do we apply them to the copy.

For near-duplicates we do not merge on a hunch. We group likely matches, explain why they look alike, and follow the choice you make about which record to keep. The Basic package handles one sheet with the standard fixes. Standard covers several sheets, near-duplicate matching and unified contact formats. Premium builds a repeatable process, as a script or set of sheet formulas, so you can run the same rules on every new export, and it can merge two lists into one.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the untouched original somewhere safe before any cleaning starts.
- Tell us which column is the unique key, such as email or customer number.
- Approve the rules before the full run, using a handful of sample rows.
- Keep the change log so any edit can be reversed.
- Fix the source form or import that creates the mess, if you can.

**Avoid:**
- Cleaning your only copy by hand with find and replace.
- Merging records by name alone, since two people can share a name.
- Deleting rows with missing values before checking whether they matter.
- Mixing cleaned and uncleaned data in the same sheet.
- Assuming a one-time clean will stay clean if the same messy export arrives again.

## Who this service is for

It suits a shop owner preparing a customer list for a new email tool. It suits a small business moving from spreadsheets to a CRM, where bad rows would be copied into the new system. It also suits an office manager who merges lists from events, orders and sign-ups and needs one reliable table.

## What we need from you

Send the file or export, in CSV, Excel or a shared sheet, together with a short note on what each column should hold. If the data is sensitive, tell us and we will work only inside the location you choose. We never need passwords. Where a sheet is shared online, you can invite us as an editor or collaborator and remove us when the work is done.
